content: {"summary":"Both the February 28 2026 and 8 August 2026 orders‑api incidents were caused by pg‑pool exhaustion due to connections being held for an unusually long time, but the triggers differed: February’s overload stemmed from month‑end order‑summary traffic, while August’s stemmed from an orders‑db‑related slowdown not tied to request volume.","likely_cause":"Long‑running queries that kept pg connections checked out until they timed out, filling the 25‑connection pools on each pod.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"February incident was caused by order‑summary requests holding connections for about 30 seconds each, exhausting the pools at month‑end","evidence_ids":["INC-0134#1"],"quote":"Each one keeps its connection checked out until its own query comes back from orders-db, about 30 seconds"},{"text":"August incident was caused by an orders‑db issue that kept connections long, not by the number of connections","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#0","INC-0182#1"],"quote":"cause: orders-db, seen in orders-api"},{"text":"The August incident description notes the trouble was how long each connection was held, not how many could be opened","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"The trouble sat in how long each connection was held, not in how many could be opened"}],"next_checks":["Identify the specific slow query(s) that ran during the August 8 2026 window","Measure average query duration for order‑summary endpoint at month‑end","Add monitoring for pool usage and connection checkout time","Review if increasing pool max would help or just increase DB load"]}
